MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  April 25, 2017

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Bucknum at 5:02 p.m., on April 25, 2017, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on April 21, 2017, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Raths
  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs
  Mayor Bucknum

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Liability Claim: Claimant - Webster, et al. Agency Claimed Against: City of Mission
  Viejo

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 p.m., Mayor Bucknum recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City
Council reconvened at 6:05 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.
City Council Minutes  1  April 25, 2017
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the Council discussed a liability claim but there was no
reportable action from Closed Session.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Proclaim April 9, 2017, To Be Mark "Ziggy" Wilczynski Day

  Mayor Bucknum issued the proclamation.

P2.  Arts Alive Presentation

  The City Council received the presentation from Cultural Services Supervisor Dru Mauer.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Al Holguin, M.V.: expressed concern with recent violence that occurred on Marguerite Parkway
near the mall and he asked what the City can do to address it.

Linda McLaughlin, San Clemente: discussed the behavior of activists who go to the offices of
State representatives and say vile things. She said they are not peaceful protesters and it is
disgusting how low people will go when they've lost an election.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: expressed concern with the City Council's plan for the civic core area and
asked why they are spending significant public funds to enhance private property. She said staff is
creating a public image that this is what members of the public are demanding and that the Minutes
are written in a biased manner to obtain a particular purpose.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  2  April 25, 2017
 1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  (1) Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of March, 28, 2017, as
  presented; and (2) approved the Minutes for the regular City Council meeting of April 11,
  2017, as presented.

3.  Check Register Dated March 31, 2017 in the Amount of $2,158.205.72

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register Dated April 7, 2017 in the Amount of $899,887.09

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Draft Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year (FY) 2017-2018 Detailing City’s Proposed
  Use of Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Funds.

  Adopted Resolution 17-14 Approving the City's Draft Annual Action Plan for Fiscal Year
  (FY) 2017-2018 detailing the City's proposed Use of Community Development Block
  Grant (CDBG) Funds and Authorizing Submission of Such Plans to the U.S. Department
  of Housing and Urban Development (HUD).

7.  Name Change for the Senior Citizen Activity Team (SCAT)

  Changed the name of the Senior Citizen Activity Team (SCAT) to Senior Corps of Retirees
  (SCOR).

8.  Notice of Completion of Animal Services Administrative Building

  (1) Certified the completion of and accepted the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorized the City
  Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the
  Faithful Performance and Payment Bonds one year an thirty-five (35) days respectfully,
  after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or
  Liens being Filed with the City; (4) authorized the payment of the final retention of
  $35,457.45 thirty-five (35) days after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion;
  and (5) approved Contract Change Order Number 2 to GPA Architects in the amount of
  $2,750.00 for additional Construction Administration Services.

City Council Minutes  3  April 25, 2017
 9.  Annual Routine Monthly Landscape and Facility Maintenance - Contract Area1

  (1) Awarded contract for the subject services to Nieves Landscape, Inc. for the period of
  July 1, 2017, through June 30, 2019, in the amount of $882,891.34; and (2) authorized
  issuance of a purchase order to Nieves Landscape, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2017,
  through June 30, 2018, in an amount not to exceed $441,445.67, pending adoption of the
  2017-2019 budget by City Council.

10.  Annual Routine Monthly Landscape and Facility Maintenance - Contract Area 4

  (1) Awarded contract for the subject services to Nieves Landscape, Inc. for the period of
  July 1, 2017, through June 30, 2019, in the amount of $660,603.80; and (2) authorized
  issuance of a purchase order to Nieves Landscape, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2017,
  through June 30, 2018, in an amount not to exceed $330,301.90, pending adoption of the
  2017-2019 budget by City Council.

11.  Annual Routine Monthly Landscape and Facility Maintenance - Contract Area 5

  (1) Awarded contract for the subject services to Nieves Landscape, Inc. for the period of
  July 1, 2017, through June 30, 2019, in the amount of $748,237.52; and (2) authorized
  issuance of a purchase order to Nieves Landscape, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2017,
  through June 30, 2018, in an mount not to exceed $374,118.76, pending adoption of the
  2017-2019 budget by the City Council.

12.  Claims Against the City - Khabazian and Alhafidh

  Rejected claims.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 6 was removed from the Consent Calendar to allow a member of the public to comment. The
item was passed with the motion to approve the Consent Calendar (above.)

6.  Agreement with Consultant SWA Group for Oso Creek Revitalization Professional
  Services

  Daniella Radu, M.V.: expressed some concern and asked questions about the Oso Creek
  revitalization project and the possibility of housing in the civic core.

  Approved agreement with SWA Group in an amount not to exceed $68,000 for Oso Creek
  Revitalization Professional Services.

STAFF REPORTS

Items 23 and 24 were taken out of order.
City Council Minutes  4  April 25, 2017
 24.  Request for Resolution in Support of an Open, Transparent Discussion Regarding the
  Financing of the Coastal Treatment Plant

  City Manager Wilberg provided a brief summary of the request from Moulton Niguel
  Water District to support MNWD's efforts to hold a meeting with the South Orange County
  Wastewater Authority regarding the Coastal Treatment Plant.

  Joone Lopez, General Manager of Moulton Niguel Water District (MNWD): asked the City
  Council to adopt the proposed resolution of support. She stated that a meeting was
  scheduled without consulting MNWD for availability and it did not allow enough time for
  the stakeholders to come together and attend. She asked that a new meeting be scheduled
  at a later time so schedules can be coordinated.

  Michael P. Dunbar, Emerald Bay Service District, Laguna Beach: expressed
  disappointment that MMWD cannot attend a meeting on Friday, April 28 and stated that
  there are customers all over south county that are concerned about this matter, not just those
  in Mission Viejo.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to adopt
  Resolution 17-15 In Support of Moulton Niguel Water District's Request for an Open
  Discussion to Resolve Financing of Coastal Treatment Plant.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

23.  Saddleback Valley Unified School District Youth Services Contract 2017-2019

  Community Services Manager Lydie Gutfeld presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to approve the
  Saddleback Valley Unified School District Youth Services Contract for 2017-2019 and
  increase participant fee by $15 per school year and $10 per summer session as
  recommended by the Community Services Commission.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  April 25, 2017
 OLD BUSINESS

The Old Business items were taken out of order.

16.  Annual Routine Tree Trimming Contract

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  The following asked that the City issue an RFP and go out to bid for this contract: Jeff
  Melin, Great Scott Tree Service and Brent Beller, Great Scott Tree Service.

  The following expressed support for the contract renewal with West Coast Arborists:
  Robert Ruiz, Secretary/Treasurer for the Orange County Labor Union and Jesse A. Segura,
  Field Representative for Laborers International Union, Local 652.

  Ron Hall, M.V.: asked why a wage increase is recommended.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: submitted a written comment recommending the City go out to bid
  on the contract.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  approve Nineteenth Amendment to the existing contract with West Coast Arborists, Inc.
  for the period of July 1, 2017 through June 30, 2019 in the amount of $1,459,481.70; and
  (2) authorize issuance of a purchase order to West Coast Arborists, Inc. for the period of
  July 1, 2017 through June 30, 2018 in an amount not to exceed $700,186.90, pending
  adoption of the 2017-2019 budget by City Council.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

13.  FY 2017-19 Revenue Projections

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas presented the staff report.

  By consensus, the City Council received and filed the report.

14.  FY 2017-2019 CIP Budget Status Report

  Budget and Purchasing Analyst Susan Knudson presented the staff report.

  By consensus, the City Council received and filed the report.

City Council Minutes  6  April 25, 2017
 15.  Annual Routine Park, Right-of-Way, and Facility Electrical/Lighting Maintenance
  and Electrical Repair

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  approve the Fifth Amendment with C&D Electric, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2017, to
  June 30, 2019, in the amount of $489,000; and (2) authorize issuance of a purchase order
  to C&D Electric, Inc. for the period of July 1, 2017, to June 30, 2018, in an amount not to
  exceed $244,500.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

17.  Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report.

18.  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  This item was deferred to the next City Council Meeting.

19.  Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  This item was deferred to the next City Council Meeting.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Mayor Bucknum

28.  Consideration of City Committee to Address the Opiate Epidemic and Drug Misuse
  Issues

  Mayor Bucknum presented her report.

  Sergeant Michael Pixomatis, OCSD Drug Liaison: discussed Sheriff Department’s efforts
  in drug abuse prevention and he expressed support for the City's proposed committee.

  The following spoke in support of the recommended action and the City's involvement in
  drug prevention efforts: Jodi Barber, M.V., Cameron Knaverhaze, M.V.; and Rhonda
  Reardon, M.V.

City Council Minutes  7  April 25, 2017
   Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Bucknum, to approve
  formation of a South County Drug Prevention Coalition to address the local addiction and
  drug epidemic issues in Mission Viejo and surrounding communities.
  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

STAFF REPORTS (Continued)

20.  Legislative Update

  City Manager Wilberg drew the Council's attention to information that was distributed
  earlier in the evening regarding proposed legislation. The matter was continued to the May
  9, 2017, City Council Meeting.

21.  Position on State Legislation

  Council Member Kelley presented the report which, she said, she originally wrote.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to
  approve the draft letters to Governor Brown and Senator De Leon, formally opposing SB
  1 and SB 54 and directed staff to amend the letter to Governor Brown to note (in the third
  paragraph) that there are funding strategies that can be adopted as an alternative to SB 1.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

22.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Update

  Battalion Chief John Abel presented the report.

25.  Resignation of Capistrano Unified School District (CUSD) Trustee Hatton-Hodson

  City Manager Wilberg presented a brief report on the vacancy on the CUSD Board of
  Trustees.

  Daniela Radu, M.V.: submitted a written comment recommending resident Julie Collier
  for the vacant position on the CUSD Board of Trustees.

City Council Minutes  8  April 25, 2017
   Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to direct
  staff to send a letter to the Capistrano Unified School District Board of Directors noting
  the City Council’s request that a special election be held to fill the vacancy of Trustee
  Hatton-Hodson (rather than filling the vacancy by appointment.)
  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

26.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities
  calendars as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk
  for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell announced that he attended the Animal Services Center open house last
week. He said that the expansion and upgrades to the facility are excellent and something the City
can be proud of. Council Member Goodell shared that his family adopted a new Dachshund, Max,
while they were there.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley congratulated La Paz Intermediate School and Principal Jean Walker for
being named a 2017 California Gold Ribbon winner and she said that La Paz was the only Mission
Viejo secondary school to receive it. She also congratulated Gail Wood, Chairman of the Marine
Adoption Committee, who was recognized with a merit award from the California Parks and
Recreation Society. Council Member Kelley shared that resident Jodi Barber gave a presentation
on the prescription drug epidemic and shared her movie Overtaken with the Community of
Character Committee. The committee is now considering how they might utilize the program and
help get it out in the community. She also outlined her attendance at recent events including Jodi
Barber’s interview with KTLA on prescription drug deaths amongst teens, the Bunny Days event,
her interview of Lesley Stahl who came to Mission Viejo to discuss her new book “Becoming
Grandma: The Joys and Science of the New Grandparenting,” the Children's Environmental Fair
and the Earth Day/Arbor Day event. In closing, Council Member Kelley reminded residents that
Arts Alive will be held on April 29 and 30 from 12:00 to 5:00 p.m.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths asked staff about Cox Communications cabling for internet service at the
Village Center across from City Hall. He said his research shows that Cox spent over $70,000
City Council Minutes  9  April 25, 2017
 installing cable yet only three businesses have signed up for service and he is concerned with Cox’s
return on investment. Council Member Raths asked the City Attorney to comment on how the City
Council term limits came about.

Mr. Curley responded that in the late 1990s a prior Council formed a subcommittee that structured
the term limit language but there is no record as to why it was planned the way it was. That City
Council put a measure on the ballot and the voters approved the term limit clause which provides
for a 365-day break before an individual can run for another term. City Attorney Curley said the
only way to alter the ordinance would be by another vote of the people.

Council Member Raths indicated that he would like to address the matter at a future time and
consider changing the language in to disallow future terms.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs said he is intrigued by the concept of changing the term limit ordinance but
in the interest of time, he would refrain from making any further comments.

Mayor Bucknum (Continued)

27.  City-Owned Wireless (Cell) Sites: Consideration of Sale of City-Owned Facilities

  Mayor Bucknum presented the report.

  City Manager Wilberg shared that at least four companies have approached the City in the
  past few months to offer to provide an analysis on potential revenue from the sale of City-
  owned cell sites.

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Sachs, to direct staff to
  generate an RFP to hire a consultant to perform an evaluation of the benefits and the
  detriments of disposing of the City-owned cell sites.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

Mayor Bucknum encouraged residents to attend that La Paz Intermediate School International
Festival on April 28, 2017, from 5:00 to 8:00 p.m.

City Council Minutes  10  April 25, 2017
 ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:03 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, May 9, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of May 9, 2017

City Council Minutes  11  April 25, 2017
